A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLWS research, with matching algorithms and retained experiments despite substantial extensions and model renaming. Text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes the readable implementation Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports original ShuffleMamba results on ImageNet-1K, ADE20K and COCO, together with probability, token-shuffling, loss and throughput analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original supervised and downstream results and adds masked-pretraining experiments, MambaMLP results and additional shuffle-schedule ablations.

M1.justification: The original SLWS permutation, restoration and linear probability schedule remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 3.3 introduces a masked feature distillation pipeline using a frozen CLIP teacher, masked Vim encoder, self-attention decoder, feature normalization and smooth-L1 loss. This substantially extends the proposed training procedure.

E1.justification: The benchmark suite remains ImageNet-1K classification, ADE20K semantic segmentation and COCO detection/instance segmentation. v2 adds actually used masked reconstruction and teacher-feature prediction pretraining tasks through MAE and MFD experiments. This extends training-task coverage within the retained visual-recognition setting; no additional benchmark dataset is reported.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 2 and 3 add ARM, contrastive/MAE-trained MambaMLP, SimMIM, MaskDistill and BEiTv2 comparisons; Figure 4 also compares MAP. ADE20K gains Vim-B and MAE ViT-L comparators. Mamba-Reg is renamed MambaR, while COCO comparator membership is retained. The improved-recipe no-shuffle control from v1 Table 5 is removed.

E3.justification: v2 adds masked-pretraining/fine-tuning protocols, MambaMLP configurations up to 662M parameters and 384x384 Vim-L fine-tuning; the 256x256 test comparison is removed. Appendix A revises reported supervised settings, including warmup from 20 to 30 epochs, learning rate from 1e-3 to 5e-4, and large-model weight decay/drop path from 0.1/0.6 to 0.15/0.7. These documented revisions do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 2 adds SLWS comparisons within MAE and MFD pretraining, extending analysis beyond supervised training. Table 7 adds decreasing-linear and exponential schedules to test schedule direction and shape. Conversely, v1's improved-recipe no-shuffle control and 256x256 generalization analysis disappear. The CLS-token ablation, loss curves and throughput analysis are retained, with throughput converted from a plot to a table.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, uncertainty error bars or statistical significance tests. v2 continues reporting point estimates; the additional results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds MFD+SLWS classification accuracies of 84.3%, 86.7% and 87.6% for base, large and huge MambaMLP models, and 53.8 mIoU on ADE20K. These involve new models/training regimes. Existing reported values also change, including Mamba-Reg-S/MambaR-S accuracy from 81.4% to 81.1%. The 256x256 results and two supervised large-model ADE20K rows are removed, while COCO scores remain unchanged after renaming.

T1.justification: v2 adds the expected teacher-student distance minimization formulation in Equation 5 and defines an exponential shuffle-probability schedule in Section 4.3. The SSM equations, original SLWS probability formulas and O(L log L) complexity argument are retained. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on scaling roughly 300M-parameter Vim through supervised training and outperforming similarly sized supervised ViTs without auxiliary data. v2 broadens the contribution to supervised and masked-pretraining regimes, explicitly adding semantic-teacher distillation and an 87.6% ImageNet-1K state-of-the-art claim. The introduction and conclusion therefore describe a substantially expanded contribution.

C2.justification: v2 newly states that spatially downsampling hierarchical Mamba architectures are incompatible with SLWS because output order cannot be restored, and explains restoration as preventing effects from propagating into later layers. It adds interpretations concerning semantic teachers, complementary benefits across training regimes and efficiency from fewer pretraining epochs. v1's interpretation of 256x256 performance as evidence about effective receptive fields is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds detailed supervised and pretraining recipes, including augmentation strengths, label smoothing, masking ratios and model-specific shuffle rates. Sections 3.3 and 4.1 specify CLIP teacher sizes and a four-block, width-512 decoder. The abstract changes code/model availability from forthcoming to available at the same URL. Documentation remains inconsistent: Section 4.1 gives a huge-model shuffle rate of 0.4, while Table A.2 gives 0.6.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially into contrastive learning, masked modeling and feature distillation, and incorporates ARM, MAP and newer Mamba research. Positioning shifts from overcoming an inability to scale Vim toward improving training and closing remaining performance gaps. The dedicated Shuffle Models discussion and its ShuffleNet, spatially shuffled convolution and Shuffle Transformer references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, conclusion and substantial method/results passages are rewritten. v2 introduces an explicit contribution list, reorganizes experiments around training paradigms, moves implementation material into Appendix A and relocates loss analysis into the main results. ShuffleMamba naming is replaced largely by Vim/MambaR names with SLWS annotations.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper with extensively restructured tables. v2 adds the MFD pipeline diagram and pretraining comparison chart. v1 Figure 2 is separated into v2 Figure 3 and throughput Table 6, the CLS-token table is transposed, and implementation tables are added in Appendix A. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added MAE/MFD comparisons and alternative-schedule tests strengthen evidence about where SLWS helps, while clearer explanations and Appendix A improve usability and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removing v1's 81.8% improved-recipe no-shuffle control, which helped isolate regularization from recipe changes, and by conflicting huge-model shuffle rates in Section 4.1 and Table A.2. The net quality improvement is therefore limited despite the substantial expansion.
